implementation: Added a pure report renderer for evaluation run ID, source training run, evaluator, data entrypoint when available, split, checkpoint step, scalar metrics, declared sample count/limit, and data identity scope.
Unknown or omitted sample counts remain unknown and are never rendered as zero. The page does not assume classification semantics and does not reinterpret custom artifacts as samples or predictions.
Failure reports retain diagnostic codes, messages, and actionable hints. Data fingerprints are shown only when explicitly present in provenance.
Coordinator registered the page module and replaced the terminal evaluate summary; both successful and failed evaluate reports now use the human renderer.

Evaluation service and optional SDK now expose a typed, evaluator-owned preview contract. `m-model evaluate --preview-samples N` requests 1–32 records; each record has a unique sample ID and finite JSON prediction/optional target, capped at 64 KiB. The service rejects unsolicited, duplicate, invalid, oversized, or over-limit records and persists valid records in the evaluation run report. Generic custom artifacts remain opaque.

The human workbench now offers an evaluate action for completed training runs with an available checkpoint. It prompts for evaluator/data factories, split, optional sample/preview limits, fingerprint and dynamic parameters, then uses the existing Command::Evaluate service.

Evaluation history offers a samples pager only for evaluate records. It displays evaluator-owned records persisted in the run report, with JSON detail view; opaque custom artifacts are never treated as predictions.

The human workbench offers an evaluate action for completed training runs with an available checkpoint. It prompts for evaluator/data factories, split, optional sample/preview limits, fingerprint and dynamic parameters, shows a readable evaluation plan, and requires explicit confirmation before invoking Command::Evaluate.

Evaluation history renders the saved metrics/provenance summary and offers a samples pager only when explicit records exist. It displays evaluator-owned records persisted in the run report, with JSON detail view; opaque custom artifacts are never treated as predictions.

backend_preview_contract.request: m-model evaluate --preview-samples N, 1 <= N <= 32 and N <= --samples when a sample limit is supplied
backend_preview_contract.record_limits: Unique visible sample IDs; finite JSON values; at most 10,000 nodes, depth 16, and 64 KiB per record; requested-count cap.
